pageCache.text:
"A culture of care and aspiration."
We are a small Church of England Primary School grounded in family values; we foster compassion, understanding and kindness. As one of the few remaining one-form entry primary schools, we ensure each child feels known and included. We welcome all into our nurturing community.
Fanoula Smith, Executive Headteacher.
Prayer and Reflection
"Shared values are explored during collective worship which is shaped by the Anglican foundation of the school. This creates meaningful moments for spiritual development." SIAMS 2023
Early Years
Our nursery room is packed with stimulating resources to support the children’s learning, including play-dough, painting & creative, water play, messy play, domestic role-play, small world, construction, maths, writing, reading and storytelling areas.
We grow our own food!
We have created an environment in our outdoor areas in which our children develop a life-long relationship with the natural world. Implemented by trained practitioners, our children get the full Forest School experience within their own school.
Join the school food revolution!
Our children learn about real, nutritious and delicious food. Our head chef, Dan, is a member of Chefs in Schools cooking fresh food from scratch every day and using nothing pre-packaged. Even the tomato ketchup and bread are made in house!
Learning in nature
Forest School is an inspirational learning process that allows children to develop confidence and skills in a natural setting. It supports play, exploration and supported risk taking.
"A vast range of extra-curricular clubs." SIAMS 2023
Our recent SIAMS inspection report highlighted our wrap-around care. ""Staff run a vast range of extra-curricular clubs providing opportunities to flourish beyond the curriculum."

Newsletters and diary dates
Newsletter archive →
Privacy Overview
Please fill out the contact form below, and we will get in touch with you

Breakfast and After-School Clubs
"Staff run a vast range of extra-curricular clubs providing opportunities to flourish beyond the curriculum." SIAMS 2023
Wrap-Around Care at St Paul with St Luke's
The school has an onsite breakfast club from 7.45am for working parents. Children can do drawing, play board games and exercise games in the hall. We are also in partnership with magic breakfast and deliver freshly cooked, healthy toast to every class in the mornings. This is now free for everyone.
The school is in partnership with Spring After School Club which is based at Bonner School and is rated outstanding by Oftsed. Bookings are made via the website springasc.co.uk
Privacy Overview

School Vision
"Love each other as I have loved you." - John 15:12
"The vision of St Paul with St Luke Church of England Primary School unites the leadership, staff, pupils and parents. The associated values it expresses are recognised and understood across a diverse and multi-faith community." SIAMS 2023
Jesus said: ‘Love one another as I have loved you’. John 15:12
We are the branch, our children the blossom, We nurture all in our community, We grow with love, learn, and flourish.
The school’s vision stems from the timeless wisdom that is John 15:12, a nurturing community where love forms the foundational ground on which our co-humanity is built enabling all to blossom. We endeavour to cultivate a learning culture where a profound sense of love, exemplified in the teaching of Jesus Christ, fosters compassion, understanding, kindness and service in the promotion of the common good.
Fanoula Smith - Executive Headteacher
Unwavering unity embraces the command of unconditional love to dissolve the ever-present barriers faced within our context, promote inclusivity, acceptance and celebration of diversity and plurality of existence. Empathy and compassion are cultivated in order to foster a deep sense of understanding of the struggles and successes of others, standing with our community through both. Inclusive excellence celebrates individuality, our children's unique gifts and talents whilst recognising, accepting and embracing diversity to empower our children to excel academically, socially and personally.
SPIRITUAL AND REFLECTIVE
As a school we want to develop the whole child which means their spiritual, moral, social and cultural development (see www.doing smsc.org.uk). We can do this by: - providing teaching opportunities to learn about themselves, others and the world around them, including the intangible - appreciating and taking into account other people’s preferences enabling - children to use their creativity and imagination in their learning - supporting children to reflect on their experiences.
CARING AND RESPECTFUL
Some of our values are about how we treat each other. You can give people respect by: - listening actively to what they say -showing respect for differences and opinions - being honest - respecting confidentiality - taking an active stance against bullying and discrimination
As a school we want to develop the whole child which means their spiritual, moral, social and cultural development (see www.doing smsc.org.uk). We can do this by: - providing teaching opportunities to learn about themselves, others and the world around them, including the intangible - appreciating and taking into account other people’s preferences enabling - children to use their creativity and imagination in their learning - supporting children to reflect on their experiences.
SPSL is part of the local community. Together we can do more than we can individually. We can support each other, share ideas and solve problems by: - working as a team - sharing good practice with each other and the local networks/partnerships - finding ways to involve parents/carers and the wider community - making positive changes and being innovative
TAKING RESPONSIBILITY
As a school we want to develop the whole child which means their spiritual, moral, social and cultural development (see www.doing smsc.org.uk). We can do this by: - providing teaching opportunities to learn about themselves, others and the world around them, including the intangible - appreciating and taking into account other people’s preferences enabling - children to use their creativity and imagination in their learning - supporting children to reflect on their experiences.
CELEBRATING INDIVIDUALITY
Inspiring, engaging and motivating our pupils is something we value highly at SPSL. We do this by: - giving praise and encouragement when deserved -using activities that inspire, challenge and extend pupils -offering an engaging curriculum which enables individuals to develop their unique potential - developing a willingness to participate in artistic, musical, sporting, mathematical, technological scientific and cultural opportunities.

Parent Activities
We hold coffee morning for parents/carers every Friday between 9am and 10am in the Father Duncan Ross Room. We look forward to seeing you there.
Privacy Overview

Reading at SPSL
We are using the Bookmark App to help children catch up with reading. Find out more here.
How we teach children to read and write
The importance of learning to read cannot be overstated. Reading develops a child's imagination, as well as empathy and self-understanding. Reading unlocks the rest of the curriculum, enabling children to get the most out of their school days and to give them the best chance for their futures.
A Reading Environment
We go to great lengths to create an inspiring atmosphere to develop a love of reading. Each classroom has its own exciting reading area. There are library clubs and public reading areas where children can read at playtimes. We give book tokens as prizes for good work and conduct.
A Systematic Approach
We use Read Write Inc, a massively successful scheme for teaching reading developed by Ruth Miskin, used in over five thousand schools around the world. Later, guided reading develops children's fluency and understanding of what they are reading. Each week has a different text focus, covering a range of fiction and non-fiction genres. Children read a differentiated text as a class, with a partner and individually. They develop their comprehension skills through answering a range of questions both verbally and in writing. They then complete activities such as sequencing pictures and information, using the text to help them. Pupils also have opportunities to read levelled books of their choice, as well as books related to their topic. This supports children's speed in reading.
As children complete the RWI programme, usually towards the end of Year 1 or beginning of Year 2, they are taught a daily guided reading lesson.
Guided reading develops children's fluency and understanding of what they are reading. Each week has a different text focus, covering a range of fiction and non-fiction genres. Children read a differentiated text as a class, with a partner and individually. They develop their comprehension skills through answering a range of questions both verbally and in writing. They then complete activities such as sequencing pictures and information, using the text to help them. Pupils also have opportunities to read levelled books of their choice, as well as books related to their topic. This supports children's speed in reading.
In Key Stage 2, as well as reading as part of our text-based Literacy curriculum, children experience a reading lesson for 30 minutes each day. The timetable for this may look like this:
The whole class are guided by the teacher to read a short text, and then answer vocabulary based questions, as well as literal, inferential and evaluative questions. We use the Reading Explorer books to support this. Teachers incorporate the 4 skills of reciprocal reading in these sessions (prediction, clarification, questioning and summarising).
Children apply their developing comprehension to read and answer questions about the text linked to their Literacy book

SEND
Special Educational Needs at SPSL
We are passionate about ensuring the very best provision for all our pupils so that no children are left behind. Our school is inclusive and able to adapt so that all children are able to flourish.
Jesus said, "I have come that you may have life in all its fullness". We embrace the whole child and enable them to flourish whether neurodiverse or neurotypical, adapting our provision so that their light is able to shine. We foster the development of wise relationships in order to promote positive identities, emotional regulation skills and executive function. We recognise that the school is not the building but is the community of people within it and that they allow transformation to take place.
Responding to the needs of our community we have a class for autistic children, called Flamingo Class, that is run by experienced specialist teachers.
SEND Local Offer
The local offer tells you what support is available from the council for children and young people with special educational needs or disabilities, and their families. It includes information about education, health and care provision. It will also tell you about training, employment and independent living for young people with special educational needs or disabilities.
Find out about the local offer at St Paul's With St Luke's on the council website here.
SEND Information Report
The school’s SEND information report informs parents and carers about how we provide for children with special educational needs and/or disabilities in our school.
It explains how we support them in all aspects of school life and remove barriers to achievement, and how we work in close partnership with parents/carers and children. You can read our latest SEND Report here.
Privacy Overview

Support and Advice for Parents
What support is there for parents and how can I support my child?
'Meet the class teacher' meetings for parents are arranged for the start of the autumn term. Parent consultations are arranged in either the end of the autumn or start of spring terms and at the start of the summer term. These meetings are helpful for parents to find out how well their child is making progress in their learning. Parents receive their child's end of year report in July and can arrange a meeting with the teacher to discuss it.
The Pastoral Team are:
SENDCo - Bremila Thavarajah
Learning Mentor - Meena Khanom
Place2Be Counsellor - Jo Gibson
They are available to meet parents for support and advice and can be contacted via the school office.
